title: PayPal
content:
## Overview

PayPal is one of the most widely-used payment processors worldwide, supporting credit cards, debit cards, and PayPal account payments. Integrating PayPal into your Emergent app enables you to accept payments from customers in over 200 markets and 25+ currencies.

This guide walks you through setting up PayPal for your Emergent project, from creating a developer account to processing your first transaction.

<Note>
PayPal offers both **Standard** (redirect-based) and **Advanced** (in-context checkout) integrations. Emergent supports both patterns — describe your preferred checkout flow in chat and the platform will scaffold the appropriate implementation.
</Note>

## Before you begin

You'll need:

- A PayPal Business account (or a PayPal Developer sandbox account for testing)
- Your app deployed or running locally in Emergent
- Basic understanding of your app's payment flow

<Tip>
If you don't have a PayPal Business account yet, you can start with a free Developer account at [developer.paypal.com](https://developer.paypal.com) — it includes sandbox credentials for testing without processing real money.
</Tip>

## Get your PayPal API credentials

<Steps>
<Step title="Log in to the PayPal Developer Dashboard">
Navigate to [developer.paypal.com](https://developer.paypal.com) and sign in with your PayPal account. If this is your first time, you'll be prompted to accept the developer agreement.
</Step>

<Step title="Create an app">
1. Go to **My Apps & Credentials** in the dashboard
2. Click **Create App**
3. Enter an app name (e.g., "Emergent Payment Integration")
4. Select the account type — choose **Sandbox** for testing or **Live** for production
5. Click **Create App**

PayPal will generate a **Client ID** and **Secret** for your application.
</Step>

<Step title="Copy your credentials">
On the app details page, copy:
- **Client ID** — your public identifier
- **Secret** — your private API key (keep this secure)

You'll use these in the next section to configure Emergent.
</Step>

<Step title="Enable required features">
Scroll down to **Features** and ensure the following are enabled:
- **Accept Payments** — core checkout functionality
- **Webhooks** (optional but recommended) — receive real-time payment notifications

Click **Save** if you make any changes.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Configure PayPal in Emergent

<Steps>
<Step title="Add credentials to your environment">
In your Emergent chat, describe where you need PayPal configured. For example:

> "Add PayPal checkout to the pricing page. Use the Client ID and Secret from my environment variables."

Emergent will prompt you for the credentials if they're not already set.
</Step>

<Step title="Set environment variables">
Provide your PayPal credentials as environment variables:

```bash
PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID=your_client_id_here
PAYPAL_SECRET=your_secret_here
PAYPAL_MODE=sandbox  # or 'live' for production
```

<Warning>
Never commit your `PAYPAL_SECRET` to version control. Emergent stores environment variables securely and injects them at runtime.
</Warning>
</Step>

<Step title="Verify the integration">
Ask Emergent to implement a test checkout flow. For example:

> "Create a button that charges $10 via PayPal and shows a success message on completion."

Emergent will scaffold the PayPal SDK integration, handle the OAuth token exchange, and create the necessary API calls.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Testing your integration

<Tabs>
<Tab title="Sandbox testing">
PayPal provides test accounts pre-configured in your sandbox:

1. Go to **Sandbox → Accounts** in the Developer Dashboard
2. Use the **Personal** (buyer) account credentials to complete test purchases
3. Check the **Business** (seller) account to verify funds were received

All sandbox transactions use fake money and cards — no real charges occur.
</Tab>

<Tab title="Live testing">
Before going live:

1. Switch `PAYPAL_MODE` to `live` in your environment variables
2. Replace sandbox credentials with your live Client ID and Secret
3. Process a small real transaction (e.g., $0.50) to verify end-to-end flow
4. Check your PayPal Business account dashboard for the incoming payment

<Info>
PayPal charges a transaction fee (typically 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction in the US). Fees vary by region and transaction volume — see [PayPal's pricing page](https://www.paypal.com/pricing) for details.
</Info>
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Common payment flows

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="One-time payments" icon="credit-card">
Standard checkout for products, services, or donations. User completes payment and returns to your app.
</Card>

<Card title="Subscriptions" icon="repeat">
Recurring billing for memberships or SaaS. Requires PayPal Billing Plan setup in your dashboard.
</Card>

<Card title="Invoicing" icon="file-text">
Send payment requests via email. Useful for B2B or custom quotes.
</Card>

<Card title="Refunds & disputes" icon="undo">
Process refunds programmatically or handle buyer disputes through the PayPal Resolution Center.
</Card>
</CardGroup>

Describe your desired flow to Emergent (e.g., *"Add a monthly subscription plan for $29/month with PayPal"*) and the platform will implement the appropriate PayPal API calls.

## Webhooks (optional)

Webhooks notify your app about payment events in real time — completed payments, refunds, disputes, subscription cancellations, etc.

<Steps>
<Step title="Enable webhooks in PayPal">
In the Developer Dashboard:
1. Go to your app's settings
2. Scroll to **Webhooks**
3. Click **Add Webhook**
4. Enter your webhook URL: `https://your-app.emergent.app/api/webhooks/paypal`
5. Select the events you want to receive (at minimum: `PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED`)
</Step>

<Step title="Implement the webhook handler">
Tell Emergent to create the endpoint:

> "Add a webhook at /api/webhooks/paypal that verifies PayPal signatures and updates order status in the database."

Emergent will scaffold signature verification, event parsing, and database updates.
</Step>

<Step title="Test webhook delivery">
Use the **Webhook Simulator** in the PayPal dashboard to send test events to your endpoint and verify correct handling.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Tip>
Webhooks are essential for subscription apps — they let you know when a renewal succeeds or fails without polling the API.
</Tip>

## Security best practices

- **Never expose your Secret** — keep it in environment variables, not in code
- **Verify webhook signatures** — PayPal signs all webhook requests; reject unsigned calls
- **Use HTTPS in production** — PayPal requires secure endpoints for live webhooks
- **Validate amounts server-side** — never trust payment amounts sent from the client

Emergent's generated code includes signature verification and server-side validation by default.

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Payment fails with 'INSTRUMENT_DECLINED'">
This is a PayPal error indicating the buyer's payment method was declined by their bank. Ask the buyer to:
- Verify their card details
- Contact their bank to authorize international transactions (if applicable)
- Try a different payment method

In sandbox mode, ensure you're using a valid test card from PayPal's test account list.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Webhooks not arriving">
Check that:
- Your webhook URL is publicly accessible (not `localhost`)
- The endpoint returns a `200 OK` status within 10 seconds
- Your app is running and not rate-limited by PayPal

View delivery attempts and retry failed webhooks in the PayPal dashboard under **Webhooks → Recent Deliveries**.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="'Client ID not found' error">
You're likely using sandbox credentials in live mode (or vice versa). Verify:
- `PAYPAL_MODE` matches your credential type (`sandbox` or `live`)
- You copied the correct Client ID for the selected mode

Each mode has separate credentials — sandbox keys won't work in production.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Refund fails with 'TRANSACTION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED'">
PayPal limits the number of refunds you can issue within a time window. If you hit this limit:
- Wait 24 hours and retry
- Contact PayPal Support to request a limit increase
- For high-volume refunds, use batch refund APIs
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Going live checklist

Before switching to production:

- [ ] Replace sandbox credentials with live Client ID and Secret
- [ ] Set `PAYPAL_MODE=live` in environment variables
- [ ] Update webhook URLs to your production domain
- [ ] Test a small real transaction end-to-end
- [ ] Review PayPal's [Go Live Checklist](https://developer.paypal.com/api/rest/production/)
- [ ] Ensure your business details are correct in your PayPal Business account

<Warning title="Data handling compliance">
If you store payment data or user information, ensure your app complies with PCI-DSS, GDPR, and other applicable regulations. PayPal handles sensitive card data, but you're responsible for protecting customer information in your database.
</Warning>

## Next steps

Store order history and customer data in your Emergent MongoDB instance
</Card>
